title: fix(cli,runtime): the ownership refusal os start prints exports the auth secret it keeps in its home
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBXyqsnJCqZ3DaKgxUVGuVM4)_

domain:server#6 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzj1WJNGVejm8mrJ71y

Fixes #29882

## What changes

- **`@objectstack/runtime`.** `OrganizationOwnershipBootGuardOptions` gains an optional `authSecretFile`: the file a production boot read its auth secret from because the operator set none. On a boot that is not a development boot, the refusal names both ceremony commands with that secret exported from the file. This covers every refusal that names the ceremony: no marker, an outdated generation, an unreadable marker, an unverified marker, a column read that failed, and a birth marker that could not be written. A path a shell would split or expand becomes one double-quoted word. One sentence says why the commands carry the secret. The `--dev` spelling does not change.

  ```
  Run 'OS_AUTH_SECRET="$(cat /srv/app/.objectstack/auth-secret)" os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN' to write and review its plan, take a backup, then run 'OS_AUTH_SECRET="$(cat /srv/app/.objectstack/auth-secret)" os migrate organization-ownership --apply --plan-file PLAN --backup-taken', and start again. Both commands export the auth secret this server read from /srv/app/.objectstack/auth-secret: the ceremony composes the security plugin only with the secret the deployment serves with, and without it the apply can stop at its authored-conversion step.
  ```

- **`@objectstack/cli`.** `os start` now tells its `serve` child where the secret came from. It uses a new internal channel, `OS_INTERNAL_AUTH_SECRET_FILE` (`utils/internal-auth-secret-channel.ts`), which follows the same naming and ownership rule as `OS_INTERNAL_ARTIFACT_PATH` and is deliberately undocumented. The parent sets the variable only when the secret came from `<home>/auth-secret`, and only when that file really holds the secret (a generated secret whose write failed lives in the process alone). Otherwise it deletes the variable, so an inherited copy never speaks for the parent. `os serve` passes the file to the guard.

- **Docs.** `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` › `os migrate organization-ownership` gains one bullet: run the ceremony with the auth secret the deployment serves with, and what an `os start` refusal names.
- **Clause-② yes (widening).** `OrganizationOwnershipBootGuardOptions` is re-exported from `@objectstack/runtime`, so the optional `authSecretFile` widens the package's public surface. It is not a protocol change, so the changeset stays `patch`.

## Why

On a v17-shaped database, `os start` refused the boot and named the ceremony bare. When the operator had set no secret, `os start` was serving with the secret it persists in its home, and that secret is not in the operator's shell. Run exactly as printed, the ceremony composed no security plugin: the plan was written and the apply stopped at `authored-conversion` ("Did not compose the security plugin…"), and nothing named the secret or where it lived. That is the card's measurement at `589049b0`. #23871 fixed the same gap for `os dev` / `os serve --dev`. This PR fixes the `os start` branch.

**Release read (asked by the maintainer):** not blocking for 18.3.0. The text has read this way since 18.0.0, so it is no regression. The stopped apply resumes from its checkpoint with no data lost once `OS_AUTH_SECRET` is exported. The changeset says that for operators who already hit it.

**Out of scope, noted:** a boot whose secret the operator passed as `os start --auth-secret X`, with no matching export, still names the bare commands. The refusal has no file to point at, and the secret must never be printed. The changeset says to run them with that secret in `OS_AUTH_SECRET`. The database URL is also not named: `os start -d URL` needs `OS_DATABASE_URL`/`--database-url` on the ceremony, as the card's own reproduction set it.

## Verification

Measured on `objectstack-ai/objectstack@00f72f94` (main at branch point) plus this branch.

- `packages/runtime` `src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.test.ts`: 23/23 pass. A new case covers the file-sourced spelling in all four refusal states, quoting of a path with a space and `$`, and the `--dev` spelling winning over a file.
- New `packages/cli/test/start-organization-ownership-refusal.integration.test.ts` (built CLI, `bin/run.js`, `NODE_ENV` unset): 5/5 pass, file wall time about 29 s locally. It boots a fresh `os start --home H`, stages the 17.x shape (`sys_secret.organization_id` plus no marker), and checks four things:
  - the refused boot names both commands with `OS_AUTH_SECRET="$(cat H/auth-secret)"`, read from the printed line, and the secret itself is never printed;
  - a boot under the operator's `OS_AUTH_SECRET` names the bare commands;
  - the two commands, run **through bash exactly as printed** in a shell with no secret, write the plan and complete the apply ("The ceremony is complete", "Security Plugin initialized", no "Did not compose the security plugin");
  - the next `os start` serves the database.
- **Reverse check:** with the channel write ablated in `start.ts` (CLI rebuilt), 2 of the 5 cases go red: the refusal names the bare commands, and the apply run as printed never initializes the security plugin. Restored from the commit, all 5 are green again.
- `pnpm typecheck` for `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/cli` (including `check:test-typecheck`): pass. `eslint` on the 6 touched source and test files: clean.
- start.ts source pins (`port-contract-single-source`, `console-route-ledger.conformance`, `child-env-source-loader.pin`, `start-port-forwarding-channel.pin`, `artifact-child-env.pin`): 69/69 pass.
- `pnpm lint` (repo-wide): exit 0.
- `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` for this change set, plus the 5 roster-adjacent gates it marks ⛔: 67 commands, 64 exit 0 on the first sweep. 3 exited 3 on a missing prerequisite, not on a finding. `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` needed its pinned fixture commit fetched into the shallow clone; once fetched it exits 0 (48 cases). `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` needed a full `pnpm build`; after it, both exit 0. The 31 docs-family gates the `cli.mdx` edit adds to the derived set also exit 0.

Clause-②: yes (widening)
